lane: LANE B6 — per-race ground integration under a built tower (exploration / options-with-consequences)
owner_item: boot-snapshot.md:38 item 4 — "Per-race ground integration under a built tower … it kinda looks like it's sticking out like a sore thumb … maybe goo for zombies, blood for vampires, cracks with fire for demons." Plus this session's "do we generate little art that we put at the base of every tower … it has to be dynamic for every race", and his point 6 tie to the tower FOOTPRINT ("for demons maybe like cracks in the ground or fire; for mummies … desert, like dunes, sand").
root_cause:
A built tower sprite is placed at the structure's live member centroid and drawn with nothing between its foot and the terrain. There is no ground-contact layer anywhere in the tree: `grep -rni "decal|scorch|stain" src --include=*.ts | grep -v test` returns only `bossAuras.ts` (the zombie-boss rot scorch) and `chewerRenderer.ts` (a death splat) — neither is attached to a structure. So a 99 px goblin tower is composited straight onto a 0.55-alpha race backdrop with a hard silhouette edge and no shadow, no contact shading, no material. That is exactly "sticking out like a sore thumb", and it is a MISSING LAYER, not bad art.

⭐ THE WHOLE JOB IS ALREADY 80% BUILT AND THE PARTS ARE IN FOUR PLACES:
1. Per-race identity: six races with a colour AND a shipped terrain identity (`races.ts:53`, `RACE_COLORS:74`, and the generation prompts in `assets-source/race-zones/design-spec.json:65-96` which name each race's ground material and accent hue in words).
2. Per-race backdrop the decal must blend INTO: `zoneBackgroundRenderer.ts`, 12 PNGs already shipped in `public/art/race-zones/`, drawn at `ZONE_BG_ALPHA = 0.55` on `groundLayer`.
3. A proven per-race PROCEDURAL Pixi module with an exhaustive `switch (raceId)`: `raceMotifs.ts` — three such functions already ship, and its test drives them through a `FakeGraphics` recorder, so a fourth is fully unit-testable without a renderer.
4. A proven ground-material procedural: `bossAuras.ts:216` `drawRotAura` is literally a goo pool — a dark scorch disc plus 14 hash-scattered bubbles on a swell/pop cycle, squashed 0.55 vertically "because the board is seen at an angle", with no `Math.random`.

So the answer to "how much of this can be procedural?" is: ALL OF IT, and the precedents are already in the repo.

fix_shape:
⭐ RECOMMENDATION UP FRONT: BUILD IT PROCEDURALLY, PUBLISHED FROM THE TOWER RENDERERS, SIZED FROM `blueprintExtent`. Zero generated art, ~300 lines, no wire change, and it makes his footprint item and his ground item the same piece of work.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
A · THE THREE OPTIONS, WITH CONSEQUENCES
═══════════════════════════════════════════

**OPTION 1 — PROCEDURAL DECAL (recommended).** A pure `drawRaceGroundDecal(g, cx, cy, halfW, halfH, tick, seed, color, raceId)` in `raceMotifs.ts`'s idiom, plus one thin renderer.
· Cost: ZERO money, ~300 lines, ~3 KiB of bundle against 147.8 KiB of headroom.
· Dynamic per race AND per tower size for free — one function serves 6 races × 18 race towers × 5 ramp towers × any future tower. An atlas would need a PNG per race per size class.
· Fully unit-testable through the `FakeGraphics` recorder (`raceMotifs.test.ts:25`) — six distinct signatures, determinism, alpha bounds. That is stronger verification than anything the atlas path can have.
· ⚠ Consequence he should hear: it will read as *stylised* — flat shapes and glows, not painted texture. Against a backdrop that is already "a faded mural seen through darkness" that is a match, not a compromise, but it is not the same register as his generated tower art.

**OPTION 2 — ATLAS DECALS (what he was offering to pay for).** One decal PNG per race, tinted/scaled per tower.
· Cost: 6 generations minimum, and realistically 6 × 2 size classes because a 68 px tier-3 ring and a 128 px tier-9 ring want different crack density. Plus the whole `ART_PIPELINE.md` stage 1-5 loop per sheet.
· ⛔ Measured argument against, from this repo: `zoneBackgroundRenderer.ts:393` records that backdrop textures killed a CI browser context at 23.7 MB and the fix was halving the art, not the code. Decal atlases are more textures on the same stack.
· ⭐ The honest case FOR it: painted texture under a painted tower is a better visual match than Graphics primitives. If he does one thing himself, this is the thing worth doing — but only AFTER he has looked at the free version.

**OPTION 3 — HYBRID (the cheap escalation path).** Ship Option 1 now; leave the draw function behind a `RACE_GROUND[race].texture: string | null` field that is `null` for all six. If he later generates one decal PNG per race, a texture path is ~20 lines and the procedural version stays as the fallback — exactly the `drawRaceKeepFallback` contract (`raceMotifs.ts:54-65`: "Ship a race-tinted procedural placeholder for any race whose art is not ready — do NOT block the wave"). ⭐ THIS IS THE ONE TO RECOMMEND TO HIM: it spends nothing today and does not throw the work away if he spends later.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
B · ITEM 5 — THE SIX DECALS, IN DRAW CALLS
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Every colour below is taken from the SHIPPED backdrop prompt for that race (`assets-source/race-zones/design-spec.json:65-96`) plus `RACE_COLORS`. Common structure, so all six read as one system: a BODY (dark, alpha ~0.30, the material), a RIM/DETAIL (the shape), and an ACCENT in the race hue (alpha ~0.35-0.5, the only bright thing). All sized from the hull box, all squashed vertically (`* 0.55`, the `bossAuras.ts:217` convention — the board is seen at an angle).

· **ZOMBIES — goo pool. CONVINCINGLY PROCEDURAL; ALREADY WRITTEN.** Lift `drawRotAura` (`bossAuras.ts:216`): one flat scorch ellipse `0x2a3d18` @ 0.28, three overlapping lobe ellipses off-centre for a lumpy edge, then 10-14 bubbles `0x7bbf3a` hash-scattered, radius 2.2-5.5, on a 42-tick swell-and-pop, plus two `0x44ff5e` @ 0.30 highlight dots as the "swamp-glow rising off the water". ~24 lines. **Best of the six.**

· **DEMONS — cracks + ember glow. CONVINCINGLY PROCEDURAL.** 5-7 `moveTo/lineTo` polylines radiating from the centroid to the hull edge, each with 2-3 hash-jittered kink points; stroke twice — once wide `0x1a1216` @ 0.5 (the fissure mouth), once narrow in the accent @ 0.45 with a tick-driven breathe. Plus one soft radial `circle` @ 0.12 as the glow bleed. ⛔ **ACCENT COLOUR IS A RULING HE OWES US** — his words say "fire", his shipped backdrop says violet-magenta `0xd73bff` in the fissures. Build it magenta (canon-consistent), expose one constant, ask.

· **MUMMIES — sand drift. CONVINCINGLY PROCEDURAL.** Three stacked ellipses of decreasing width, offset downwind on a fixed per-structure angle from `mix32(anchorId, 0)`, filled `0x6b5a44` @ 0.22 / 0.16 / 0.10 — a dune shoulder banked against the tower's foot. Add ~8 `circle(r 1.2)` grains at `0xffe23b` @ 0.18 along the leeward edge. Static; sand does not animate. ~18 lines.

· **VAMPIRES — blood pool. CONVINCINGLY PROCEDURAL.** One dark ellipse `0x3a0e18` @ 0.34, two smaller spatter ellipses at hash-fixed offsets outside the hull, and a thin `0xff3b6b` @ 0.40 meniscus arc along the lower rim (the wet edge is what makes it read as liquid rather than a shadow). Static, or a very slow ~180-tick sheen. ~16 lines.

· **ORCS — trampled hardpan. CONVINCINGLY PROCEDURAL.** A `roundRect` of the hull filled `0x3a2a1e` @ 0.20, then 6-8 short `lineTo` scuff strokes at hash angles @ 0.14, plus two `0xff8c1a` @ 0.25 ember dots as the "low banked cook-fires". Static. ~16 lines. ⚠ The weakest of the six as a *concept* — "churned dirt" is a subtle read at this size. If one race justifies real art, it is this one.

· **NAGAS — silt wash + tide pool. CONVINCINGLY PROCEDURAL.** A wide `0x12303a` @ 0.24 ellipse, two concentric arc strokes `0x3bd7ff` @ 0.22 offset by a slow `world.tick` phase (a lapping current, the "cyan shimmer on the drifting silt"), and 4-5 small darker pebble ellipses. ~18 lines.

**VERDICT ON WHICH WANT ART:** zombies, demons, vampires and nagas are convincingly procedural — they are liquids, glows and cracks, which is what Graphics primitives do well. Mummies is borderline (a sand DUNE has a lit face; flat fills fake that poorly). Orcs is the one genuine art candidate. So the honest answer to give him is **"four for free, one probably fine, one you may want to draw"** — not "all six for free".

═══════════════════════════════════════════

and its `.sync(world)` immediately before `structureRenderer.sync(world)` at `main.ts:3989`.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
D · ITEM 4 — THE FOOTPRINT LINK. ⭐ SAY THIS LOUDLY: ONE FUNCTION ALREADY SERVES BOTH.
═══════════════════════════════════════════
`blueprintExtent(recipeId)` (`blueprints.ts:483`) returns `{minDx, maxDx, minDy, maxDy}` — the true per-side footprint including `FOOTPRINT_MARGIN` 12. It is ALREADY the space placement refuses to overlap (`stampFootprintBox`, `blueprintLegality.ts:62`) and ALREADY the rectangle the carried-tower ghost outlines (`blueprintGhost.ts:105`). Draw the decal in that box, at the structure's live centroid, and:
· the decal is EXACTLY the ground the tower claimed — his "towers should take the space that it takes their connectors to be on";
· the player sees the same rectangle while placing and after building;
· it cannot drift from the art, because `structureRamp.ts:233-275` already derives every tower's art size from the same radii.
⚠ ONE HONEST CAVEAT: `blueprintExtent` is BLUEPRINT-space (the stamp's ideal offsets). A built structure's shapes drift a little as Verlet settles, so the live members' bounding box is a few px off the ideal. Two answers, both fine: (a) use the blueprint box centred on the live centroid — stable, never wobbles, and is the same box placement used; (b) compute a live box from `rampMembersAt(...).members` / `ringMembersAt(...)`. ⭐ Take (a): a decal that breathes with Verlet jitter would look like a bug, and (a) needs no new walk.

⛔⛔ **WORKTREE COLLISION, FLAGGED.** `src/state/blueprints.ts` and `src/state/blueprintLegality.ts` are lane A3's (buildable area) files. THIS LANE MUST NOT EDIT THEM — it only imports `blueprintExtent` and `blueprintFor`. If A3 changes `FOOTPRINT_MARGIN` or the extent arithmetic, this lane's decal follows automatically, which is the correct coupling. Merge A3 first, then this.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
E · ITEM 6 — DETERMINISM
═══════════════════════════════════════════
No `Math.random`. Variation seeds from the structure's anchor `PrimitiveId` through `mix32(anchorId, k)` (`rng.ts:86`) or the render-local `(k * 2654435761 + id * 40503) >>> 0` (`bossAuras.ts:223`). Animation phase from `world.tick` only — never `performance.now()` — because this is something two players watch happen to the same structure (`towerCover.ts:82`). Pure function of `(cx, cy, hull, tick, anchorId, race)`; no module state, no RNG stream, nothing on the wire, `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 47.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
F · THE PUBLISH QUESTION — TWO SHAPES, PICK B
═══════════════════════════════════════════
**A (cheapest, riskiest):** the decal renderer walks `world.creatureSpawners` + `world.defenders` itself and re-derives "a tower stands here". ~1 new file. ⛔ `towerCover.ts:17-26` documents precisely why this fails: five gates can stop a sprite (no art, fogged, atlas loading, ring unresolved, ring empty) and a re-derivation paints a goo pool on bare ground in all five.
**B (recommended):** add `markTowerGround(cx, cy, halfW, halfH, raceId, seed)` to `towerCover.ts`, using the SAME double-buffer `beginTowerCoverFrame` already runs (`towerCover.ts:149-170`). One line at each of the three existing publish sites (`towerRenderer.ts:313`, `structureRampRenderer.ts:223`, `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576`), all three of which already have the centroid in scope. The decal then appears and disappears with the sprite by construction, and gets the ±1-frame lag the module already documents and accepts. ⚠ B means the decal renderer's `.sync` must run AFTER `beginTowerCoverFrame` (`main.ts:3981`) — it does, at 3989.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
G · WHAT TO PUT IN FRONT OF HIM
═══════════════════════════════════════════

2. The demon accent colour question (his "fire" vs his backdrop's magenta) and the mummy one (seat yellow vs backdrop amber-gold).

determinism_risk:
NONE-RENDER-ONLY. No sim state, no wire field, no hash entry, no four-sites obligation, and `PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 47 — the decal reads only `world.primitives`, `world.bonds`, `world.creatureSpawners`, `world.defenders` and `player.raceId`, all already required and fully synced, and writes nothing. This is the identical argument `zoneBackgroundRenderer.ts:43` makes for the backdrop.

THREE RENDER-SIDE DETERMINISM OBLIGATIONS THAT STILL BIND:
1. No `Math.random` anywhere in the draw — variation seeds from the anchor PrimitiveId through `mix32` (`rng.ts:86`) or the render-local `(k * 2654435761 + id * 40503) >>> 0` idiom (`bossAuras.ts:223`). `constants.ts:1337` states the rule.
2. Animation phase rides `world.tick`, never `performance.now()` — this is something two players watch happen to the same structure (`towerCover.ts:82`).
3. ⛔ THE ONE REAL HAZARD, AND IT IS NOT A DESYNC: the decal must not be drawn for a tower whose sprite was NOT committed. Re-deriving "a tower stands here" disagrees with the renderer on five documented gates and paints a decal on bare ground (`towerCover.ts:17-26`). Option B in `fix_shape` removes the hazard structurally.

⚠ AND A LEAK THAT IS NOT DETERMINISM BUT IS WORSE IF MISSED: since S170 fog is a per-entity CULL, not a layer mask (`concealment.ts:502`). A decal renderer that omits its own `isConcealed` call marks every enemy tower's position through the fog, reversing the S169/S170 rulings, and no existing test would see it.
art_cost:
NO-ART — and the no-cost path is genuinely the good path here, not merely the cheap one.

WHY ZERO GENERATION IS NEEDED:
· The per-race PALETTE and GROUND MATERIAL are already written down, per race, in `assets-source/race-zones/design-spec.json:65-96` — the words that generated the twelve shipped backdrops. Reading them is free and guarantees the decal blends into the art it sits on.
· The per-race PROCEDURAL MODULE already exists with three shipped functions and an exhaustive-switch contract (`raceMotifs.ts`). A fourth costs no new structure.
· The ZOMBIE GOO POOL IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND SHIPPED — `drawRotAura` (`bossAuras.ts:216`) is a scorch disc plus hash-scattered swelling bubbles, vertically squashed for the board angle. Re-pointing it at a structure centroid is the zombie decal.
· A procedural decal is DYNAMIC PER RACE AND PER TOWER SIZE FOR FREE. An atlas is a combinatorial bill: 6 races × at least 2 size classes (a 68 px tier-3 ring and a 128 px tier-9 ring want different crack density), each through the full `ART_PIPELINE.md` stage 1-5 loop.
· And this repo has a MEASURED reason to avoid more textures on this stack: `zoneBackgroundRenderer.ts:393` records a four-seat board decoding 23.7 MB of backdrop and killing a CI browser context; the fix was halving the art, not the code.

WHAT ART WOULD BUY, STATED HONESTLY SO HE CAN DECIDE:
· Painted texture under a painted tower matches register better than Graphics primitives. Four of the six (zombies, demons, vampires, nagas) are liquids/glows/cracks and read fine as primitives. Mummies is borderline — a sand dune has a lit face that flat fills fake poorly. **Orcs (trampled hardpan) is the one genuine art candidate.**
· ⭐ THE RECOMMENDATION THAT COSTS HIM NOTHING TODAY: ship the procedural version behind a `RACE_GROUND[race].texture: string | null` that is `null` for all six. If he later draws one PNG per race himself, the texture path is ~20 lines and the procedural version survives as the load-failure fallback — exactly the contract `raceMotifs.ts:54-65` already states for the race keeps.

Bundle: ~3 KiB against 147.8 KiB of headroom (`check-bundle-size.mjs:19`, `CAP_KIB = 1000`). Zero new fetches, zero new textures.
tests_owed:
⚠ NO RENDERER RUNS UNDER VITEST — Helga drew on top of her own hall with the whole suite green. Here is what can and cannot be pinned, stated honestly.

⭐ WHAT CAN BE PINNED FOR REAL (a behavioural test, not a source-text guard):
`src/render/raceGround.test.ts`, using the `FakeGraphics` recorder at `raceMotifs.test.ts:25` — a fake `Graphics` that records op order and numeric args and produces a comparable `signature()`. That gives genuine assertions:
· all six races draw SOMETHING and no two signatures are equal (the real failure mode: a race falling through the switch and drawing nothing, which `tsc` only catches because of the `const unhandled: never` arm);
· calling twice with identical args yields an identical signature, and the module source contains no `Math.random` and no `performance.now` — determinism, proven behaviourally not by grep;
· two different anchor ids yield DIFFERENT signatures — the per-structure variation actually varies;
· every `alpha` passed is within the blend budget (≤ ~0.5), so a decal can never out-shout a 0.55-alpha backdrop;
· the drawn extent is inside `blueprintExtent(recipeId)` for every registered ramp and race recipe, derived from the live table rather than from copied literals — so a recipe retune moves the decal or turns the test red.

⚠ WHAT CAN ONLY BE PINNED AS SOURCE TEXT, WITH ITS LIMIT STATED:
· Z-ORDER. `structureRamp.test.ts:726-741` must gain `new GroundDecalRenderer(` and assert it precedes `new SparkRenderer(`, `new StructureRenderer(`, `new TowerRenderer(`, `new VoltkinTowerRenderer(` and `new StructureRampRenderer(`. Its own comment already names the limit: "A source-text guard proves a line EXISTS. It cannot prove the line is REACHED", and "a renderer added to `fogHiddenLayer` between them is the case it cannot see". Copy the S182 mechanical-enumeration pattern where possible: assert the decal is the FIRST `new *Renderer(app, fogHiddenLayer)` in the file, not merely "before these five" — a positional claim is harder to defeat by inserting a sixth renderer.
· THE FOG GATE. A `countOf(src, 'isConcealed(')` ≥ 1 in `groundDecalRenderer.ts`. ⛔ This proves the line exists, NOT that the skip is reached before the draw — exactly the hole S182 documented. The stronger version: extract every `.fill({` / `.stroke({` call in the file and require the count to match a pinned number, so a seventh draw added outside the gate turns it red (the S182 footer-band pattern, five opaque fills pinned).
· THE CENSUS LISTS. `towerCover.test.ts:267-320` iterates hand-written filename arrays for publishers and consumers. A new renderer is in neither and is therefore silently exempt — the branch must add itself, and that addition is itself part of what a reviewer should check.

⚠ WHAT NEEDS PLAYWRIGHT, AND ONE THING THAT WILL NOT WORK:
One `@races`-tagged spec (that lane exists for backdrops and settings toggles; `src/ci.e2eLanes.test.ts` pins the mapping): build one tower solo, assert exactly one decal is drawn. ⛔ THE `zone-backdrop.spec.ts` TRICK DOES NOT TRANSFER — it asserts a NETWORK REQUEST for a PNG, and a procedural decal issues none. ⛔ AND COUNTING LAYER CHILDREN DOES NOT WORK EITHER — the recommended design is ONE shared `Graphics` cleared per frame, which has zero children. So the renderer needs an explicit test seam: a `drawnCount` getter exposed as `__SPARK__.groundDecalCount`, following the named-getter convention `hub-ramp-art.spec.ts:41` insists on over `children[15]` ("a hardcoded index into a hand-maintained display list, which is why it keeps breaking"). Assert 0 before the tower is built and 1 after.

⛔ WHAT NOTHING IN THIS REPO CAN PIN, AND SAY SO TO HIM: whether it LOOKS integrated. No test judges a frame. The only verdict on "does it still stick out like a sore thumb" is his eyes on the live board, and the branch should ship with that stated rather than implied.
